elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 7.7: "The Issuer, as the customer for the Servicer's services, may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience..." The election is unconditional and therefore a true convenience right. There are no Order Forms in this servicing structure, so the Agreement-level right is the full scope available. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" reads false only because the operative party name is "Issuer" rather than a listed alias; the clause expressly identifies the Issuer as "the customer for the Servicer's services," and the resolved definitions confirm the Issuer is the recipient of the Servicer's services, so the element is satisfied in substance.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly 30 days, in writing, running from notice to the Servicer.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7: "in which case the Servicer will refund pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), payable by the Servicer (Vendor), and triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 (retained unamended): "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." Resignation conditioned on legal inability, supported by an Opinion of Counsel, is not a convenience right; no other provision permits Servicer-initiated no-fault exit. Section 7.2(c) removal is a Customer-side/Indenture Trustee for-cause mechanic, not a Vendor convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 sets 30 days' notice, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (though more favourable to us). Read literally, the fallback element is not satisfied; this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not arise: neither the retained text nor new Section 7.7 imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on the Issuer's exit, so there is no fee requiring a cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation altogether absent legal inability, so the Servicer has no convenience exit at any point, let alone mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — the Servicer holds no convenience termination right under Section 7.1, so no notice floor is engaged.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the inserted Section 7.7 supplies an unconditional Issuer (Customer) convenience right, 30 days' written notice, and an express pro rata refund of prepaid fees, while retained Section 7.1 already forecloses any Servicer convenience exit.

Targeting preferred rather than fallback is correct here: the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end convenience exit on 90 days' notice that Section 7.1 currently forbids, so proposing the fallback would worsen our position.

Minimality holds. The insertion is concise and tracks the model language while properly dropping the surplus "in whole or in part" (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists). The only other edit — Section 8.3's "earlier"→"earliest" plus "a termination under Section 7.7" — is a necessary conforming change; without it the retained natural-expiry formula ("will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a)... and (b)...") would contradict the new exit. No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or other extra was added.

Intent preserved: for-cause removal in Section 7.2(c), the successor-servicer and continued-performance mechanics (which operate on termination "under this Agreement"), Cellco's Section 3.4/4.7 acquisition obligations, and Section 7.6 succession provisions all survive unchanged and without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Drafting nit only (not a defect requiring repair): the amended Section 8.3 now reads "the earliest to occur of a termination under Section 7.7, (a)... and (b)...", leaving the first item unlettered. Consider relettering as (a), (b), (c) for tidiness; the provision is operative as written.

Note for the cover note: the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" check returned false purely because the clause names the "Issuer" rather than a playbook alias; the clause expressly designates the Issuer as "the customer for the Servicer's services," so no operative repair is needed.
